questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, it was crucial to be in a transnational environment where I could deepen my knowledge of church history and gain a broader understanding of the key figures surrounding Martin Luther, and Martin Luther himself. It was also important for me to participate in the Reformation Day celebrations in Wittenberg

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We arrived and were welcomed by a well-informed lady, and everything went smoothly

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Where to study. Where to have classes. Where to sleep. Where to eat. Additionally, we were provided with a very good map with all interesting events marked on it

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCPH, the teaching style was more inclusive.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Everything is well organized
2: All participants are in good hands.
3: Although the program is ambitious, it is possible to complete all required readings due to scheduled reading hours.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: In case of injury (as in my own experience), there is a hospital located nearby, and the host institution is very helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I am very grateful that, through teaching and discussions with fellow students, I have studied Luther through a transnational lens, which has made my understanding of Luther more nuanced and strengthened

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the paperwork before, during, and after the exchange has been quite challenging, due to the extensive documentation required and the numerous emails from various correspondents.
